prompt: 選出最適合填入空格的字。
text: Her emails were models of ___: never more than two lines, yet they always contained everything the reader needed.

wrong.verbosity: verbosity 是囉嗦，但 never more than two lines 說明很簡短，剛好相反。
wrong.ambiguity: ambiguity 是含糊不清，句中說內容包含讀者所需的一切，表示清楚而非含糊。
wrong.pedantry: pedantry 是賣弄學問、拘泥小節，與簡短又完整的信件沒有關係。

why: never more than two lines 又包含全部資訊，就是簡潔精準的 concision。
tip: short but complete 就是 concise 的家族。
say: Her emails were models of concision.

prompt: 選出最適合填入空格的字。
text: The lecturer's ___ digressions stretched a twenty-minute talk into a two-hour ordeal.

wrong.laconic: laconic 指言簡意賅，無法解釋為何講座會被拖長。
wrong.pithy: pithy 是簡練有力的，同樣與拖長的效果相反。
wrong.terse: terse 是簡短而略顯生硬，與 stretched into a two-hour ordeal 互相矛盾。

why: 離題使演講從二十分鐘變成兩小時，需要形容冗長無盡的 interminable。
tip: 拖長的結果會告訴你要選冗長的字。
say: His interminable digressions stretched the talk.

prompt: prolix 這個字最接近下列哪個意思？
text: The contract was so prolix that even the lawyers struggled to find the key clause.

wrong.精簡扼要的: 如果合約精簡，律師就不會難以找到關鍵條款，意思相反。
wrong.艱澀古老的: 句子沒有提到用語古老，prolix 的重點是字數過多。
wrong.偽造的: 沒有任何線索指出合約造假，這是憑空猜測的意思。

why: 律師連關鍵條款都難找，表示文字太多、太冗長，prolix 就是這個意思。

prompt: 哪一句用 laconic 最恰當？
options: Asked about his weekend, the laconic farmer simply answered, "Fine."
The laconic speech lasted three hours and covered every detail.
She gave a laconic and rambling account of her trip.
The laconic report ran to six hundred pages of footnotes.
answer: Asked about his weekend, the laconic farmer simply answered, "Fine."

wrong.The laconic speech lasted three hours an: 三小時又包含每個細節是冗長，與 laconic 的簡短相反。
wrong.She gave a laconic and rambling account: rambling 是東拉西扯，與 laconic 自相矛盾。
wrong.The laconic report ran to six hundred pa: 六百頁註腳是長篇，不是簡短。

why: laconic 形容話少，只回答一個 Fine 就是最典型的例子。
tip: laconic 是話少；別和冗長的字放一起。

prompt: 主編要你把稿子刪到最精簡，哪一句最適合回報成果？
options: I trimmed the draft to its essentials without losing any key point.
I padded the draft with extra examples to make it fuller.
I made the draft more circuitous so readers stay longer.
I kept every sentence because nothing was redundant at all, but added more.
answer: I trimmed the draft to its essentials without losing any key point.

wrong.I padded the draft with extra examples t: pad 是灌水加長，與主編要求精簡相反。
wrong.I made the draft more circuitous so read: circuitous 是繞圈子，只會讓文章更不精簡。
wrong.I kept every sentence because nothing wa: 一邊說保留全部，一邊又增加內容，沒有完成刪減。

why: 精簡就是去掉多餘內容、保留重點，trim to essentials 正好說明。
say: I trimmed the draft to its essentials.

prompt: 選出最適合填入空格的字。
text: The poet is admired for her ___ style: a single carefully chosen image can carry an entire stanza.

wrong.bombastic: bombastic 是誇大華麗，與只用一個意象承載整段不合。
wrong.redundant: redundant 是多餘重複，而句子稱讚的是精簡有力。
wrong.discursive: discursive 是漫談離題，和單一意象濃縮全段的特色相反。

why: 用最少文字承載最多意義，就是用字經濟的 economical。
tip: 文學評論的 economical 指用字精省而有力。
say: She is admired for her economical style.

prompt: 這句話表達的意思是什麼？
text: Brevity is the soul of wit, but brevity without clarity is merely obscure.
options: 簡短很好，但若不清楚就只是晦澀
簡短永遠比清楚更重要
answer: 簡短很好，但若不清楚就只是晦澀

wrong.簡短永遠比清楚更重要: 句子 but 之後強調簡短要有清晰，並未說簡短永遠優先。
wrong.機智的人不需要說話: 句子談的是簡潔與機智的關係，沒有說不需要說話。
wrong.清楚的話一定很冗長: 句中沒有這個因果，作者要求的是又短又清楚。

why: but 的後半句補上條件：簡短必須清楚，否則只會讓人看不懂。
tip: but 後面常是作者想強調的限制條件。
say: Brevity without clarity is merely obscure.
